description: Stats track only (design 3.2, no audio). Each case lists report snapshots in arrival order and the expected stats intervals (stage 3 'intervals' columns) and the five stats flags of 800 consecutive probe chunks (as runs of ones, [first chunk, count]) [t_media + 32 ms i, t_media + 32 ms (i + 1)), i = 0..799, after the rules of stage 3 (t_media_ns is the tap clock at media start). A null counter is an absent field. Times are int64 ns; req_ns, arrive_ns and oldest_ns are on the tap clock; report_ns is on the UTC clock and is used only to drop a duplicate delivery.

cases.name: steady
cases.description: no anomaly: every interval known, the reference for the other cases; the two guard intervals close the ends

cases.name: first_burst_before_sample
cases.description: the first request is at 1.000 s and audible concealment runs from 0.960 to 0.990 s, just before the first sample (about 1.003 s): it is in the baseline of the counters and in no delta, and the sample is only known to lie in [req - 50 ms, arrive]. The guard interval [0.950, arrive_0) is unknown, so the chunks inside it are concealment-unknown (without it interval 1 would call them clean)

cases.name: first_sample_late
cases.description: the first request is at 1.000 s but the worker thread samples at 1.800 s (callback 1.815 s); audible concealment 1.1 to 1.5 s is in the baseline, in no delta. Guard interval [0.950, 1.815) unknown (interval 1 spans it and is known)

cases.name: last_callback_late
cases.description: the track ends at snapshot 24 (request 24.5 s, sampled 24.502 s) and its callback runs 1.2 s after the request (below late_ms); audible concealment 24.3 to 24.9 s is partly after the last sample, in no delta. Guard interval [24.450, arrive_24) unknown, and nothing is known after it

cases.name: worker_busy
cases.description: the worker thread is busy for 0.4 s at snapshot 10: request 10.5 s, counters sampled at 10.9 s, callback 10.915 s. Audible concealment 10.65 to 10.85 s lies before the sample, so it is counted in interval 10, whose span runs to the callback: the interval end is the arrival, never the request or a report timestamp

cases.name: join_foreign
cases.description: the request at 8.5 s joins a collection that another getStats caller on the same PeerConnection started at 7.8 s (that caller's request is outstanding: oldest_ns 7.8 s); the counters were sampled at 7.803 s, 0.697 s before the request, and the callback runs at 8.8 s. Audible concealment 7.9 to 8.2 s is counted in interval 9, which therefore starts at the oldest outstanding stamp (7.8 s) and not at req - cache_ms (8.45 s)

cases.name: dup_delivery
cases.description: the app's own timer fires again at 13.5 s while the collection of the request at 12.5 s is still in flight (its callback runs 1.3 s after its request): the second request joins it and is delivered right after with the same report timestamp and the same counters. The duplicate is dropped (a zero-length interval would reset the TX floor to -120 dB) and interval 13 spans from the first request to the next report: it is 2 s long, and so is its TX window (d(tx_duration_s) above tx_span_ms), so it is unknown, as with a missing report

cases.name: playout_stall
cases.description: nothing is played between the reports 12 and 13 (hold): report 13 has a new timestamp but all ten counters equal those of report 12, and the later counters lost that second; the tap counted nothing either (a gap in the tap track without a jump of its position). Not a duplicate: interval 13 is known with zero deltas

cases.name: same_report_other_counters
cases.description: reports 12 and 13 carry the same report timestamp but different counters: not a duplicate, both are used

cases.name: report_clock_step
cases.description: the UTC clock steps forward by 0.8 s at report 12 and back by 2.8 s at report 20 (report times go backwards): the report timestamp is never used for timing, so every interval, flag and column equals the steady case

cases.name: out_of_order
cases.description: the callbacks of reports 13 and 21 run before those of reports 12 and 20 (1.45 s after their requests): the file lists them in arrival order, the engine orders by request time, so the span of interval 12 (20) ends after that of the interval that follows it. Interval 12 has audible concealment and a chunk near the end of its span is touched only interval 21 (audible concealment) ends exactly at 21.500 s, so the chunk [21.600, 21.632) (widened start through it; interval 21 (audible concealment) ends exactly at 21.500 s, so the chunk [21.600, 21.632) (widened start 21.500 s) is not touched by it. The TX power is -56 dBFS except in interval 13, where it is -42.88 dBFS: the floor there is the floor after interval 12 (-54.78 dB, which rose by 1.21 dB over the 2.42 s between the arrivals of reports 11 and 12) minus 0.20 dB, because the arrival of report 13 is 0.40 s BEFORE that of report 12 (the elapsed time between arrivals is negative and the floor falls: threshold -42.98 dBFS, active); a floor that only rises (the elapsed time clamped at 0) has the threshold at -42.78 dBFS and calls it inactive

cases.name: req_boundary
cases.description: request 13 is stamped exactly like request 12 (requests must strictly increase: interval 13 unknown) and request 21 one ns after request 20 (known)

cases.name: malformed_stamps
cases.description: snapshot 13 arrives one ns before its request and snapshot 17 has an oldest outstanding stamp one ns after its own request (neither can happen on one clock): both are dropped and the intervals across them are 2 s long, with a TX window of 2 s (above tx_span_ms): unknown, as with a missing report; snapshot 21 arrives exactly at its request (valid) and is kept

cases.name: echo_overlap
cases.description: the overlap of two spans puts tEnd + post_ms in two intervals with different look-backs: interval 10 has a jitter buffer delay of 1.7 s (pre 2098 ms), 9 and 11 are at the 1000 ms floor, 15 again has 1.7 s and 16 is at the floor. TX is active in interval 7 (6.6 to 7.4 s) and in interval 13 (12.6 to 13.4 s): a chunk whose end lies in the overlap of 9 and 10 (or of 15 and 16) is excluded or not by the LARGEST look-back of the two, whichever comes first

cases.name: span_edges
cases.description: spans are half-open and the widening is 100 ms: interval 9 (audible concealment) ends exactly at 9.500 s, so the chunk [9.600, 9.632) (widened start 9.500 s) does not overlap it and is clean, and interval 13 (audible concealment) starts exactly at 12.900 s, so the chunk [12.768, 12.800) (widened end 12.900 s) does not overlap it and is clean

cases.name: late_boundary
cases.description: callback 10 runs exactly 1500 ms after its request (not above late_ms: known) and callback 20 exactly 1501 ms after (unknown); each makes the next callback follow it (one thread, delivered in order) without making it late

cases.name: late_run_known
cases.description: 16 callbacks (10 to 25) each exactly 1400 ms after their request (a loaded thread): every interval is known, each spans about 2.5 s and overlaps its neighbours by about 1.5 s, so the concealment of the steady track is attributed to more chunks, never fewer

cases.name: late_run_unknown
cases.description: the same at 1600 ms (above late_ms): intervals 10 to 25 are unknown, the others are placed as in the steady track

cases.name: late_burst
cases.description: the signalling thread blocks for 2.2 s at report 14: its callback (above late_ms) is late and reports 15 and 16 are delivered one behind the other after it (1.2 s and 0.2 s after their requests: known)

cases.name: missing_report
cases.description: report 20 never arrives: the interval between reports 19 and 21 is [lo_19, arrive_21), 2.1 s long, inside span_ms, but the TX power it reports is an average over 2 s (above tx_span_ms): unknown. The TX power is -56 dBFS except -42 dBFS in the second between the samples of reports 20 and 21, which alone is active (threshold about -43.5 dBFS); averaged over the two seconds it is -44.8 dBFS, inactive. Without the TX window bound the interval would be known and inactive and the chunks over the burst would be neither excluded nor TX-unknown

cases.name: receiver_restart
cases.description: the inbound counters restart from zero at snapshot 15 (the receiver was re-created) while the stamps advance normally: interval 15 is unknown, interval 16 is known again

cases.name: sender_restart
cases.description: the outbound counters (energy, duration) restart from zero at snapshot 15: interval 15 is unknown

cases.name: stream_replaced
cases.description: the audio inbound-rtp row of snapshot 15 and the later ones has another SSRC (the inbound stream was replaced; the counters of a young new stream can already exceed the old ones, so no delta is negative): interval 15 is unknown, interval 16 is known again

cases.name: absent_fields
cases.description: absent counters (null): all inbound counters in the first two reports (no inbound-rtp row yet), the media source counters in report 8, and one counter (jb_emitted) in report 20: the intervals that use them are unknown

cases.name: silent_over_concealed
cases.description: delta(silent_concealed) = 480 above delta(concealed) = 0 in interval 15: doubtful, so unknown (the app helper audibleConcealed would clamp it to 0; the engine must not). Interval 18 has the two equal (silent-only concealment): known, audible 0

cases.name: tx_levels
cases.description: TX power given per interval (dBFS, see TX_LEVELS in voicelab/statscases.py): the margin of 12 dB above the noise floor (-44.0 inactive, -43.0 active), the rise of the floor per second of elapsed tap time between ARRIVALS (callback 8 is 1.0 s late, so 2.0 s pass before it and about 0 s after), a loud run of six intervals, and the absolute limit of -50 dBFS (-50.5 inactive, -49.5 active)

cases.name: span_bound_missing_reports
cases.description: reports 20 and 21 never arrive: the interval between reports 19 and 22 is [lo_19, arrive_22), 3.1 s long, above span_ms (2600), with a TX window of 3 s (above tx_span_ms): unknown. The TX power is -56 dBFS except -42 dBFS in the second of the missing report 21, which alone is active (threshold about -43.5 dBFS); averaged over the three seconds it is -46.4 dBFS, inactive. Without the bound the interval would be known and inactive and the chunks over the burst would be neither excluded nor TX-unknown (here either bound alone decides; span_boundary pins the span bound alone, tx_span_boundary the TX window bound)

cases.name: span_boundary
cases.description: the poll of request 10 slips to 1050 ms after request 9 and its callback runs exactly 1500 ms after the request (late_ms: trusted): the span [lo_9, arrive_10) is 50 + 1050 + 1500 = 2600 ms, exactly span_ms: known. Request 20 is 1 ns later than 1050 ms after request 19 with the same callback delay: 2600 ms and 1 ns, unknown, although its callback is not late

cases.name: tx_span_boundary
cases.description: the counters of report 10 are sampled 1749.5 ms after those of report 9 and those of report 20 1750.5 ms after those of report 19 (a worker thread that samples late; the callbacks are not late and the spans are 1.8 s): the TX power of the interval is an average over d(tx_duration_s) = 1749.5 ms (tx_span_ms 1750: known) and over 1750.5 ms (unknown). The bound is on the window of the average, not on lateness

cases.name: tx_late_known
cases.description: callback 5 runs 1450 ms after its request (trusted: below late_ms; its span is 2.5 s, below span_ms) and report 5 carries a TX burst (-40 dBFS in a track at -56 dBFS): the TX window is still the 1 s between the samples, so the interval is known and TX-active. Lateness widens the span, never the window of the TX average

cases.name: join_missed_by_registry
cases.description: as join_foreign (the request at 8.5 s joins a collection another caller started at 7.8 s; counters sampled at 7.803 s) but the app's registry did not see that caller, so oldest_ns = req_ns and the span of interval 9 starts at 8.45 s: the audible concealment 7.9 to 8.2 s is in no span that counted it. The tap tells: NetEq counted 0.3 s between reports 7 and 8 where the tap counted 1.27 s, and 1.7 s between 8 and 9 where the tap counted 0.73 s, so intervals 8 and 9 are unknown

cases.name: recreated_same_ssrc
cases.description: the inbound stream is re-created at 0.9 s with the same SSRC (a young stream: its counters restart from zero, and 0.6 s later, at report 1, they are still above those of report 0, so no counter went backwards and rx_ssrc did not change): NetEq counts 0.1 s between reports 0 and 1 where the tap counted 1.0 s, so interval 1 is unknown, and the offset between the counters jumped by 0.9 s; interval 2 is known again

cases.name: tap_offset_drift
cases.description: NetEq counts 60 ms fewer samples than the tap from reports 6, 9 and 12 on (a counter discontinuity of 2880 samples each): one step is below the allowance of the delta check (the two spans of the interval, 20 ms of lag and 20 ms of tolerance) and of the offset check (this interval's span plus 40 ms); the second makes the offset 120 ms below the largest offset seen, so the offset check marks interval 9 unknown and restarts the bound; the third is one step again

cases.name: tap_drop_between_arrivals
cases.description: the worker queue drops the tap blocks between 14.70 s and 15.30 s (400 ms of queue overflow, 60 blocks); the tap callback counted them before the queue, so the position of the next block includes them and the span between the arrivals of reports 14 (14.53 s) and 15 (15.53 s) still holds 1.0 s: every interval is known. A port that counts the blocks it received instead sees 0.6 s too little and marks interval 15 unknown

cases.name: tap_drop_over_arrival
cases.description: the worker queue drops the tap blocks between 14.00 s and 15.05 s and report 14 arrives at 14.53 s inside the gap: the position the engine knows at that arrival is the one of the last block before the gap (14.00 s), 0.53 s too low, so intervals 14 and 15 are unknown (the tap cannot tell where it was), and so is interval 13, whose counters look 0.53 s too old next to the stale position of report 14 (the one-ahead comparison)

cases.name: tap_delta_boundary
cases.description: NetEq counts more samples than the tap from report 8 on, by 9744 samples (203 ms) at report 8 and by 8689 samples (181 ms) at report 18, the largest jumps that the delta check allows there being 9744 and 8688 (the spans of the two reports and of the one before, plus 40 ms): interval 8 is known, interval 18 is unknown (one sample, 20.8 us, over). The intervals before the jumps, 7 and 17, are unknown as well: a jump this size is above what the one-ahead comparison allows (tap_ahead_boundary)

cases.name: tap_offset_boundary
cases.description: NetEq counts 4848 samples (101 ms) fewer than the tap at report 8, the largest drop of the offset that the offset check allows there (the span of the report plus 40 ms): known; the offset is restored at report 9 (a gain of 101 ms is inside the delta check). At report 18 the drop is 5041 samples, one over the 5040 allowed there: interval 18 is unknown, and the offset is restored at report 19. (A drop that is not restored is tested again by every later report against the largest offset seen, with a smaller allowance each time.)

cases.name: tap_ahead_boundary
cases.description: NetEq counts more samples than the tap from report 9 on, by 5088 samples at report 9 and by 5809 at report 19: the one-ahead comparison marks the interval BEFORE a jump up when the next offset exceeds this one by more than the span of this report plus 40 ms (a report whose counters are older than its bracket looks like that), the delta check the interval of the jump itself only above the spans of both reports plus 40 ms. At report 9 the jump is the largest one that keeps interval 8 known, at report 19 one sample (20.8 us) more: interval 18 is unknown; the intervals 9 and 19 are known

cases.name: tap_arrival_on_block
cases.description: reports 8 and 18 are delivered exactly on a tap block (8.600 s and 18.600 s: the callback of that block is at that instant), and NetEq counts 4656 (report 8) and 4657 (report 18) samples fewer than the tap there, restored at the next report. The tap position at an arrival is the one of the last block called AT OR BEFORE it, so the block that is called at the arrival counts: 4656 samples is the largest drop the offset check allows at report 8 (known), one sample more at report 18 is unknown. A position that excludes the block at the arrival (10 ms less) or one that takes the next block (10 ms more) moves the limit by 480 samples

cases.name: tap_end_on_arrival
cases.description: the track ends at report 19, which is delivered exactly at the last tap block (19.600 s: the tap is still defined there), and NetEq counts 20000 samples (0.42 s) fewer than the tap at it: the offset check and the delta check run and interval 19 is unknown. A tap that is taken as ended at its last block would skip report 19 and call it known

cases.name: tap_end_skips_predecessor
cases.description: the tap ends at 13.700 s. Report 12 is delivered 1.4 s after its request, at 13.900 s, after the end of the tap (the checks skip it); report 13 is delivered at 13.550 s, before it (the file lists it first), and NetEq counts 20000 samples (0.42 s) more than the tap from report 13 on. Report 13 has no checked predecessor (the one before it was skipped, and the delta check does not look past a skipped report) and the offset check only looks for drops, so interval 13 is known. A port that compares report 13 with report 11 sees the jump and marks it unknown

cases.name: hidden_concealment_event
cases.description: an audible concealment event at 14.3 s whose samples a merge correction cancelled (NetEq's negative correction after an earlier merge is subtracted from this event): concealmentEvents moves by 1, concealedSamples and silentConcealedSamples do not. Interval 14 has audible 0 and silent 0 and events 1: it touches concealment, so the chunks within 100 ms of its span are touch_conc (a rule on the sample counters alone would call them clean)

cases.name: muted_tail_hidden_event
cases.description: a long loss from 10.6 s to 12.49 s that NetEq has muted (silent samples; its event is counted in interval 11) and an audible event at 12.2 s whose samples the merge correction that ended the loss cancelled: interval 12 holds the muted tail (silent samples), no new event of the loss, and the hidden event: audible 0, silent > 0, events 1. It touches concealment (a rule that lets silent samples in the interval switch the event off would call the chunks around 12.2 s clean, with the event in the same interval as the tail)

cases.name: dtx_silent_concealment
cases.description: four concealment events with silent (comfort noise) samples only, as an Opus DTX gap would produce (the apps negotiate no DTX, docs E2): concealmentEvents moves and silentConcealedSamples with it, so audible is 0 and each of the four intervals still touches concealment (an event counts whatever its samples are: over-flagging a DTX gap costs availability only, missing a hidden event next to a muted tail would cost the verdict)
